import jobs

def test_stable_first_occurrence_wins():
    rows = [
        {'title': 'Job A', 'source': 'src1', 'source_id': 'id1'},
        {'title': 'Job A', 'source': 'src1', 'source_id': 'id2'},  # same title, different source_id
        {'title': 'Job A', 'source': 'src1', 'source_id': 'id1'},  # duplicate of first
    ]
    result = jobs.unique_jobs(rows)
    assert len(result) == 2, f"Expected 2 unique rows, got {len(result)}"
    assert result[0]['title'] == 'Job A'
    assert result[0]['source_id'] == 'id1'


def test_do_not_merge_across_sources():
    rows = [
        {'title': 'Job A', 'source': 'src1', 'source_id': 'id1'},
        {'title': 'Job A', 'source': 'src2', 'source_id': 'id1'},  # different source
    ]
    result = jobs.unique_jobs(rows)
    assert len(result) == 2, f"Expected 2 unique rows (different sources), got {len(result)}"


def test_do_not_merge_by_title():
    rows = [
        {'title': 'Job A', 'source': 'src1', 'source_id': 'id1'},
        {'title': 'Job B', 'source': 'src1', 'source_id': 'id2'},  # different title
        {'title': 'Job A', 'source': 'src1', 'source_id': 'id3'},  # same title as first, different source_id
    ]
    result = jobs.unique_jobs(rows)
    assert len(result) == 3, f"Expected 3 unique rows (different source_ids), got {len(result)}"


def test_missing_source_id_kept_separately():
    rows = [
        {'title': 'Job A', 'source': 'src1', 'source_id': 'id1'},
        {'title': 'Job B', 'source': 'src1', 'source_id': None},  # missing source_id
        {'title': 'Job C', 'source': 'src1', 'source_id': ''},    # empty source_id
    ]
    result = jobs.unique_jobs(rows)
    assert len(result) == 3, f"Expected 3 unique rows (all have different (source, source_id)), got {len(result)}"


def test_none_source_kept_separately():
    rows = [
        {'title': 'Job A', 'source': 'src1', 'source_id': 'id1'},
        {'title': 'Job B', 'source': None, 'source_id': 'id2'},  # None source
    ]
    result = jobs.unique_jobs(rows)
    assert len(result) == 2, f"Expected 2 unique rows (different sources), got {len(result)}"


def test_do_not_mutate_input():
    rows = [
        {'title': 'Job A', 'source': 'src1', 'source_id': 'id1'},
        {'title': 'Job B', 'source': 'src1', 'source_id': 'id2'},
    ]
    original_rows = [dict(row) for row in rows]
    result = jobs.unique_jobs(rows)
    assert result == rows, "Result should match input when no duplicates exist"
    
    # Check that original rows are not mutated
    for orig, res in zip(original_rows, result):
        assert orig == res, "Input rows should not be mutated"


def test_empty_source_id_treated_as_unique_key():
    rows = [
        {'title': 'Job A', 'source': 'src1', 'source_id': ''},
        {'title': 'Job B', 'source': 'src1', 'source_id': None},
        {'title': 'Job C', 'source': 'src1', 'source_id': 'id1'},
    ]
    result = jobs.unique_jobs(rows)
    assert len(result) == 3, f"Expected 3 unique rows, got {len(result)}"


if __name__ == '__main__':
    test_stable_first_occurrence_wins()
    print("test_stable_first_occurrence_wins passed")
    
    test_do_not_merge_across_sources()
    print("test_do_not_merge_across_sources passed")
    
    test_do_not_merge_by_title()
    print("test_do_not_merge_by_title passed")
    
    test_missing_source_id_kept_separately()
    print("test_missing_source_id_kept_separately passed")
    
    test_none_source_kept_separately()
    print("test_none_source_kept_separately passed")
    
    test_do_not_mutate_input()
    print("test_do_not_mutate_input passed")
    
    test_empty_source_id_treated_as_unique_key()
    print("test_empty_source_id_treated_as_unique_key passed")
    
    print("\nAll tests passed!")
